parameters.query:
-- The unique index on (provider, provider_event_id) is what actually stops a
-- double enrolment. Two concurrent deliveries of the same event both run this
-- INSERT; Postgres lets exactly one of them create the row and the other gets
-- zero rows back from ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. No application-level check can
-- give that guarantee.
INSERT INTO processed_events (provider, provider_event_id, event_type, payload)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb)
ON CONFLICT (provider, provider_event_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id, received_at;

parameters.query:
-- One statement so the enrolment row and the ledger update either both land or
-- neither does. A crash between two separate writes would leave the event marked
-- processed with no enrolment behind it.
WITH upserted AS (
  INSERT INTO enrolments (
    provider_event_id, email, course_id, thinkific_user_id, thinkific_enrolment_id, state
  )
  VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
  ON CONFLICT (provider_event_id) DO UPDATE
    SET thinkific_enrolment_id = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.thinkific_enrolment_id, enrolments.thinkific_enrolment_id),
        state = EXCLUDED.state,
        updated_at = now()
  RETURNING id, provider_event_id
)
UPDATE processed_events p
   SET status = 'completed',
       completed_at = now()
  FROM upserted u
 WHERE p.provider_event_id = u.provider_event_id
RETURNING u.id AS enrolment_id, p.provider_event_id;
